cluster_summary: A set of vulnerabilities where user-supplied input (column names, sort directions, WHERE fragments, native function references) is directly concatenated into SQL or HQL queries without being validated against a whitelist of allowed values or safe identifier rules. This allows injection of arbitrary SQL syntax leading to SQL injection.
guideline_text: Trace lower-privilege script, template, macro, plugin, or API callers that can invoke privileged server-side capabilities into server-side include, template rendering, servlet dispatch, raw object access, internal file reads, or privileged framework APIs. Report code paths where a higher privilege check is not enforced at the API entry point before exposing the server-side capability. Confirm that the required guard is enforced on the same source-to-sink path before the sensitive effect. Treat this as a reusable mechanism-level pattern derived from 1 historical CVE example(s), not as a project-specific signature. A safe implementation should check the required higher privilege at the exposed API boundary and return no sensitive result when the caller lacks that privilege.

mechanism.missing_guard: a higher privilege check is not enforced at the API entry point before exposing the server-side capability
mechanism.name: privileged server-side capability exposed to lower privilege context
mechanism.sink_shape: server-side include, template rendering, servlet dispatch, raw object access, internal file reads, or privileged framework APIs
mechanism.source_shape: lower-privilege script, template, macro, plugin, or API callers that can invoke privileged server-side capabilities
mechanism.typical_fix: check the required higher privilege at the exposed API boundary and return no sensitive result when the caller lacks that privilege

sub_patterns.fix_strategy: Complete short HQL forms to full SELECT statements, validate the resulting statement using a safety parser (e.g., HqlQueryUtils.isSafe) that checks against whitelisted patterns, and reject dangerous metacharacters like '--' or semicolons in WHERE clauses.
sub_patterns.name: Unvalidated HQL/SQL query fragments (WHERE, short forms)
sub_patterns.root_cause: The code treats user-supplied query fragments (WHERE clause, short HQL forms like 'where' or 'order by') as safe without completing them to a full statement or validating their syntax against a safety filter, allowing injection of arbitrary SQL/HQL constructs.
